purpose: Landmark-compatible constraint system for selecting the canonical shoulder girdle without fitting back to the r95 mesh.

lateral_acromion_to_AC_joint_mm.definition: straight distance from lateral acromion to AC joint

clavicle_endpoint_length_mm.definition: straight 3D distance between lateral-most clavicular point in AC joint and medial-most clavicular point in SC joint

derived_constraints.note: The last value is a consistency check only. Real SC-to-AC separation has AP and vertical components, so final SC/AC coordinates must satisfy the full 3D chord.

hard_geometry_rules: each_SC_to_AC_3D_chord should lie in an endpoint-length adult-male corridor after stature/sex context is reconciled
AC and GH remain distinct centres
lateral acromion remains lateral to AC joint
left/right canonical geometry is mirrored except where an explicit asymmetry policy is applied
acceptance_logic: Reject any candidate whose bi-AC breadth exceeds the outer biacromial breadth.
Reject any candidate whose SC-to-AC straight chord exceeds the clavicle curved centreline length.
Reject any candidate requiring the lateral acromion-to-AC offset outside the registered adult range without a documented reason.
Do not force the scapular GH-to-inferior-angle span to a value until the 3D scapular landmark frame is solved.
Do not move the whole shoulder vertically just to repair width: acromial height is already close to the stature-conditioned scaffold.
interpretation: The old a003 shoulder width is not just visually broad; the current bilateral AC breadth (~481 mm) is larger than the expected OUTER biacromial breadth (~425 mm), which is anatomically impossible as a normal target because AC joints sit medial to the lateral acromial points.
Using the population mean inputs gives a provisional bilateral AC breadth around 357 mm. This is a constraint-derived centre, not yet a frozen production target.

The mean inputs are internally coherent with a bilateral SC breadth around 48 mm if the clavicle chord were purely lateral; adding AP/Z offsets means the final target will need a slightly different combination inside the allowed corridors.
next_steps: Solve SC/AC/acromion coordinates in 3D against the clavicle endpoint/centreline constraints and global shoulder-height scaffold.
Build the scapular local landmark frame independently, then place GH from the retained local depth and glenoid geometry.
Rerun shoulder-complex solver tests after the canonical girdle coordinates are instantiated.
